newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada resists U.S. pressure to cap grain exports.
newsitem.headline: Canada resists U.S. pressure to cap grain exports.

text.p: U.S. officials are under pressure to persuade Canada to limit its grain exports, but Ottawa will not budge in its refusal, Canadian government officials said on Friday after meeting with their U.S. counterparts.
"They're under a fair amount of political pressure to put pressure on us, and they're doing their job," foreign ministry spokesman Charles Larabie told Reuters.
While Canada will continue to meet with American officials on the issue, it will not change its mind on limiting grain exports, Larabie said in a telephone interview.
"They can ask until the cows come home," he vowed.

Farmers in the northern U.S. plains and some politicians have complained of an unfair level of Canadian wheat exports. The Clinton administration has told Canada it would take action if the shipments exceeded 1.5 million tonnes a year -- a level Canada is close to reaching in the crop year ending July 31.
Senior officials will likely meet again in late summer to discuss grain exports and other issues, Larabie said.
The United States may be looking to increase its own grain exports to Canada rather than push for a cap on Canadian grain exports, officials said.
Canada's biggest province, Ontario, imported U.S. grain this year after its own crop was lower than expected.
Canada's grain exports are high because of strong U.S. demand, they said, noting that there are no barriers to U.S. farmers wanting to sell their grain in Canada.
"There are a lot of myths out there," said one official. "There's a lot of need for dialogue."
In 1994-95, Canada agreed to cap annual grain exports at 1.5 million tonnes a year after much of the U.S. crop was destroyed by flooding. But that agreement has expired.
